To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) abstract brand concepts are representations of human values; (b) cultural congruity and compatibility between values matter for the acceptability of brand concepts; and (c) cultural compatibility between values is more important for brand concept acceptability than cultural congruity.

the proposed brand concept structure (1) can predict which brand concepts are likely to be more (less) accepted when added to an existing brand concept, (2) can predict the cultural compatibility of brand concepts, (3) is robust across different countries, (4) is useful for predicting consumer responses to changes in brand meanings, (5) is robust across product categories, and (6) is robust across consumer groups.

(1) the structure of abstract brand concept is a useful tool for predicting the compatibility of brand concepts and the congruity of these concepts to cultural values, and (2) these predictions can be made based on the cultural orientations of consumers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that cultural congruity between values plays in consumers’ responses to abstract brand concepts.
the question of what makes a global brand successful across borders.
the question of whether and how cultural congruity and compatibility matter for the success of global brands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed framework of abstract brand concepts is particularly useful for understanding and predicting how consumers respond to global brands and their concepts.
this paper shows that brand concepts as representations for human values are useful for predicting consumer reactions to brand concepts in different cultural contexts.
the proposed structure of abstract brand values is a useful tool for understanding and predicting the impact of cultural congruence and compatibility on brand concepts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed structure of abstract brand meanings as representations of human value is useful in predicting how consumers from different cultural backgrounds will respond to brand concepts that are (in)congruent with their own values.
brand managers should consider the compatibility between the values that their brands represent and the values held by their customers, as these are important drivers of brand success.
brand concepts are more favorably received when they are culturally congruent and conceptually compatible with each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
brand meanings are not just about what the brand does, they are also about what the brand stands for and, more importantly, what they stand for in the eyes of the consumers.
abstract brand concepts can be used to convey human values and that the cultural congruity and compatibility between these values and those of the consumer can be leveraged to enhance brand meaning.
abstract brand concepts are not only useful for building brands, but also for understanding how brands are perceived and evaluated in the minds of consumers.
